label: first input token is i (t=0)
explanation: Fires exactly at step t=0 when the first original token is the letter i, and nowhere else. On the dev split precision, recall and F1 are all 1.0. Magnitude is constant (0.101 on every activation), so nothing modulates it; L, digit count and later tokens make no difference. It does not fire on i at later original positions, at the delimiter, or in the copy phase, including when i is being output at recall_idx 0 (the step after <DEL>).

issues: None found. Dev profile: active on 16781 steps, every one at t=0 / orig_idx=0. Zero activations at the delimiter, in the copy phase, at any recall_idx (including 0) or at any t>=1. Magnitude is constant: mean, median and max are all 0.101.
Test split: precision 1.0, recall 1.0, F1 1.0, mass recall 1.0, correlation 1.0 (n_active = n_predicted = 16679). misses --split test shows 0 missed activations and 0 false positives.

L only shifts the per-step rate because sequences have different lengths. Firing counts per L are about the same (around 2.7k for each L from 5 to 9), which fits a dependence on the first token alone.

Minor note, not a refutation: at t=0 the hidden state is always the initial state, so the gate input depends only on the token. A perfect response to one token at t=0 is therefore expected, and the feature is a deterministic lookup of first-token i.
